title: Sharad Pawar, Supriya Sule Meet PM Modi as NCP-NDA Merger Speculation Intensifies
excerpt: The meeting in Parliament during the monsoon session has fuelled fresh speculation about Sharad Pawar's NCP faction potentially joining the ruling NDA alliance.
body:
• NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar and working president Supriya Sule met PM Modi in Parliament during the monsoon session, triggering intense speculation about a possible NDA alignment.
  • The BJP-led NDA is actively seeking a two-thirds majority to pass constitutional amendment bills on delimitation and women's reservation, and remains 42 seats short in the Lok Sabha.
  • Reports suggest the NDA has proposed reuniting both NCP factions with two Union Cabinet posts as inducement, though no formal announcement has been made.
  • Senior NCP (SP) leaders have publicly denied merger talks, insisting the party remains united behind Sharad Pawar.

NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) chief Sharad Pawar and party working president Supriya Sule met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Parliament on Tuesday, setting off a fresh round of speculation about the opposition party's possible shift toward the ruling NDA.

The meeting came during the monsoon session and amid intensifying political activity in Delhi. Neither side has officially disclosed the substance of the discussions.

Weeks of Backroom Buzz

The Pawar-Modi meeting caps a series of encounters that have kept Maharashtra's political circles on edge. On July 8, Pawar met Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde at the Vidhan Bhavan in Mumbai — his first visit for a meeting on the Maharashtra-Karnataka border dispute in 28 years. Days later, NCP (SP) leader Jayant Patil's late-night visit to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis's residence 'Varsha' added to the chatter, even as Patil insisted it was about a local constituency matter.

The Two-Thirds Imperative

The backdrop is the NDA's push to secure a two-thirds majority in both houses of Parliament for constitutional amendment bills on delimitation and the Women's Reservation Act — efforts that failed during a special Rajya Sabha session in April.

"We are all united behind Sharad Pawar. It saddens me that the media continuously cooks up such speculative stories."

— Jayant Patil, NCP (SP) leader

Since then, the NDA has expanded aggressively. In June 2026, 20 Lok Sabha MPs joined the NDA-backed Nationalist Citizens Party. Six of nine MPs from Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena faction crossed to the Shinde faction. The NDA's Lok Sabha tally stands at 318 — 42 short of the 360 needed. In the Rajya Sabha, the NDA holds 152 seats, 11 short of 163. The NCP (SP)'s eight Lok Sabha MPs could meaningfully close that gap.

The Merger Proposal

According to media reports, the NDA leadership has floated a proposal for both NCP factions — the Sharad Pawar faction and the Sunetra Pawar faction already in the ruling alliance — to reunite as a single party and join the NDA. Two Union Cabinet positions have reportedly been offered.

The Sharad Pawar faction is divided. Some leaders favour the NDA, with discussions said to include a Union ministerial post for Supriya Sule. Others prefer merging with the Congress. Pawar's grandson Rohit Pawar is reportedly opposed to any NDA alignment. On the other side, Rajya Sabha MP Parth Pawar has pushed for his mother Sunetra Pawar to become the reunified party's national president.

MVA Under Strain

The speculation has strained the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi alliance. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut criticised Pawar after the Shinde meeting, questioning why a veteran opposition leader would sit in the office of someone he accused of toppling the previous MVA government.

What Comes Next

Official denials continue. NCP (SP) Maharashtra president Shashikant Shinde has called the reports "baseless." Fadnavis himself has stated no new parties are entering the NDA. Supriya Sule has expressed conditional support for the Delimitation Bill — a softer stance some analysts read as a potential opening for broader cooperation.

But the frequency of cross-party meetings suggests the conversation is far from over. With the monsoon session underway and critical constitutional amendment bills on the agenda, whether Sharad Pawar will break with his lifelong ideological positioning or use the speculation as leverage remains the central political question of the season.

nri_angle: A potential NCP realignment could reshape India's parliamentary arithmetic on key legislation including delimitation, which affects the political representation of states with large diaspora populations.
